meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Костян, ты не боишься, что Настя отнесёт шейху заказ?
examples.trans: Kostyan, are you not afraid that Nastya will take the order to the sheikh?
Well, is it ready? I will serve it myself.
Wait, are you Russian?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ваш шеф-повар раздел меня и домогался.
examples.trans: And your head chef undressed me and harassed me.

examples.text: Она угрожала рассказать, что я её раздел?
examples.trans: She threatened to say that I undressed her?
What is happening here?

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'исходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is happening', paired with 'произойти'.

examples.trans: What is happening here?
What is going on? I don't understand.

examples.text: Мы не знаем, что с нашей дочерью происходит!
examples.trans: We don't know what is happening with our daughter!

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, this is our electrician.

examples.text: Извините, я ничего не видел, пойду всё переделаю.
examples.trans: Excuse me, I saw nothing, I will go redo everything.
Excuse us, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А вот это тот самый состоятельный гость.
examples.trans: And this is that very wealthy guest.

examples.text: Так клянусь, мне повар знакомый рассказывал.
examples.trans: I swear, a cook I know told me.

examples.text: В смысле, Настя, ты мне нужна!
examples.trans: I mean, Nastya, I need you!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: Excuse us, please.
Excuse us, please!
A coffee, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Excuse me, this is our electrician.

examples.text: А вот это тот самый состоятельный гость.
examples.trans: And this is that very wealthy guest.

examples.text: В прошлом году этот шейх тоже приезжал в Москву.
examples.trans: Last year this sheikh also visited Moscow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ваш шеф-повар раздел меня и домогался.
examples.trans: And your head chef undressed me and harassed me.

examples.text: Ваш муж хочет навестить вас после ужина.
examples.trans: Your husband wants to visit you after dinner.
It is your interpreter's fault.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'водчик'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'interpreter / translator' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It is your interpreter's fault.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть переводчик.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always interpreter.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('at fault, guilty').

examples.trans: It is your interpreter's fault.
It's your fault!

examples.text: Я ни в чём не виноват.
examples.trans: I'm not to blame for anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They can rent the entire hotel.

examples.text: Он продал этот перстень и уехал за границу.
examples.trans: He sold that ring and moved abroad.

examples.text: Теперь она живёт в его гареме.
examples.trans: Now she lives in his harem.

meanings.en: to use, make use of, utilize
meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'пользовать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'uses'.

examples.text: Каким образом мы можем это использовать?
examples.trans: How can we use that?
To make use of an opportunity.

examples.text: Ты используешь нас ради своей власти!
examples.trans: You are using us for the sake of your power!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'name' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он использует ваше имя в своих целях.
examples.trans: He is using your name for his own purposes.
Let's find out the winner's name.
What is your name?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The hotel is geared toward well-off people.

examples.text: Только обеспеченный человек снимет у нас номер.
examples.trans: Only a wealthy person will book a room with us.
A truly prosperous guest will treat himself to a suite.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'one's own', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Take a look at your own face.

examples.text: Я ей свой мобильник дала на всякий случай.
examples.trans: I gave her my cell phone just in case.

examples.text: Он использует ваше имя в своих целях.
examples.trans: He is using your name for his own purposes.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'goal, aim, target' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Она уже целый час не отвечает.
examples.trans: She has not answered for a whole hour already.

examples.text: Он использует ваше имя в своих целях.
examples.trans: He is using your name for his own purposes.
We have a grown-up goal.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'ask for', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.trans: I apologise.
He's asking for help.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'щение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'forgiveness' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I beg your pardon, he will be fired.
I apologise.
He is asking me to forgive him.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'fired', paired with 'увольнять'.

examples.trans: It is a good thing we were not fired.
You're fired!
He was fired.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: We will cook it better than anyone right now!

examples.text: Слушай, сейчас шеф получит наш перстень.
examples.trans: Listen, now the Chef will get our ring.

examples.text: Всё понятно, сейчас шейха напоят, а он их отблагодарит.
examples.trans: Everything is clear, now they will get the sheikh drunk and he will reward them.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'said', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Тогда мне придётся рассказать, что ты меня напоила.
examples.trans: Then I will have to say that you got me drunk.

examples.text: Она угрожала рассказать, что я её раздел?
examples.trans: She threatened to say that I undressed her?

examples.text: Не знаю, сказала, на часик в «Метрополь» съездит.
examples.trans: I do not know, she said she would go to the Metropol for an hour.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Одна девушка отнесла ему заказ и пропала.
examples.trans: One girl brought him an order and vanished.

examples.text: А как ты посмотришь, как я запою, если ты уйдёшь?
examples.trans: And how will you see what tune I sing if you leave?
I brought the ice cream.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The hotel is geared toward well-off people.

examples.text: И больше этого официанта никто не видел.
examples.trans: And nobody ever saw that waiter again.

examples.text: Так клянусь, мне повар знакомый рассказывал.
examples.trans: I swear, a cook I know told me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'виниться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'apologize', paired with 'извиняться'.

examples.trans: I said sorry, didn't I?
Apologise to Dad.

examples.text: Ну что ты, Филиппович. Я же извинился.
examples.trans: Oh, come on, Filippovich. I said sorry, didn't I?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Только обеспеченный человек снимет у нас номер.
examples.trans: Only a wealthy person will book a room with us.
A truly prosperous guest will treat himself to a suite.
But there are very wealthy guests.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'guys, team' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Excuse us, guys, we are leaving already.
Guys, where are you?
The boys will have a word with you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Помоги как-нибудь, я уже год в гареме.
examples.trans: Help me somehow, I have been in the harem for a year already.

examples.text: Ой, спасибо тебе, я уже год так не расслаблялась.
examples.trans: Oh, thank you, I have not relaxed like this in a year.
It is time for me to go back to the kitchen.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are leaving', paired with 'уйти'.

examples.trans: Excuse us, guys, we are leaving already.
I'm going home.
You are. Go away.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I cannot return his feelings.
Sit with me a little longer.
Timur, you will drive with me to the Metropol.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such a thing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Так клянусь, мне повар знакомый рассказывал.
examples.trans: I swear, a cook I know told me.
Can you imagine how much such a ring costs?

examples.text: Нам бы тоже не помешал такой подарок.
examples.trans: We could use a gift like that too.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'вториться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will repeat', paired with 'повторяться'.

examples.trans: They are asking to repeat the ice cream for the room.
This will not happen again.

examples.text: Ошибка не должна повториться в будущем.
examples.trans: The mistake must not repeat in the future.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Представляю, но ничем не смогу помочь.
examples.trans: I can imagine, but I cannot help you with anything.

examples.text: А может, ты сможешь мне помочь?
examples.trans: Or maybe you can help me?
I can't today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'звращаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to return', paired with 'вернуться'.

examples.trans: You may return to work.
He always comes home late.
Evil always comes back.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Только обеспеченный человек снимет у нас номер.
examples.trans: Only a wealthy person will book a room with us.
A truly prosperous guest will treat himself to a suite.
Excuse me, this is our electrician.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'work' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: All staff members must work perfectly.

examples.text: Я на нашей работе такой камень могу только в почках заработать.
examples.trans: At our job I can only earn a stone that big in my kidneys.
Go work, daydreamer.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: Let us hurry to the kitchen.

examples.text: Извините, я ничего не видел, пойду всё переделаю.
examples.trans: Excuse me, I saw nothing, I will go redo everything.
Let us go check the corridor.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'сюда').

examples.trans: Get lost!
Let us get out of here to the kitchen quickly.
I'll get out of here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корее').

examples.trans: Let us hurry to the kitchen.
Help me quickly!
Louis, come here quickly!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The hotel is geared toward well-off people.

examples.text: Только обеспеченный человек снимет у нас номер.
examples.trans: Only a wealthy person will book a room with us.
Excuse me, this is our electrician.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: Let us hurry to the kitchen.
It is time for me to go back to the kitchen.
Let us get out of here to the kitchen quickly.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It is a good thing we were not fired.
Everything's fine.
Good! Everything's fine over there.
